How | “Cheated” My Way Into FAANG

Interviews and Got the Offer

Alright, so let's be real—FAANG interviews are more

about playing the game than being the best

engineer. | didn’t grind 500 LeetCode problems, and
| didn't have a perfect resume. Instead, | hacked the
interview process by understanding how hiring

actually works. Here's exactly what | did:

Step 1: Skipping the Black Hole (Cold

Applications Are a Waste)

+ | never applied through company portals. They
get thousands of applications, and ATS filters out
most of them.

+ Instead, | targeted engineers and hiring managers
on Linkedin and asked for referrals.

+ [kept my messages short and to the point: “Hey
[Name], I'm really interested in [Team/Company]
and I'd love to apply. | have [X years] of
experience in [Relevant Skill], and | think I'd be a
great fit. Would you be open to referring me?”

+ This got me multiple referrals in a week, and |
went straight to recruiter screens instead of
waiting in the void.

Step 2: Only Studying What Actually Gets Asked

+ Instead of grinding hundreds of LeetCode Me
problems, | reverse-engineered the interview
questions:
